units.function: Unit tests routing newly blocked Issues to an explicitly named Agent owner with transition-scoped idempotency and rollout compatibility.
units.dependencyDirection: Blocked Issue state/unblock descriptor enters a notification service; injected wakeup and mark-notified callbacks update scheduler and Issue delivery state.
units.keyDataModels: Issue blocked status, unblock owner Agent ID/action, blockedTransitionAt, notifiedAt, rollout timestamp and issue-unblock idempotency key.
units.lifecycle: Post-rollout blocked transitions wake the named Agent and mark delivery; pre-rollout Issues are untouched, a notified transition deduplicates, and a later blocked flap creates a new transition-keyed notification.
units.testAssessment: Tests cover prospective rollout, deterministic idempotency and repeated transitions. Missing are human owners/escalation, invalid/inactive owner, wake failure versus mark ordering, concurrent delivery, outbox durability, timeout/SLA, action validation and authorization to assign unblock ownership.
units.designRationale: Turn blocked from a passive status into routable work without flooding old records or duplicate wakes.
units.companyOsProblem: Agent Boss needs explicit blocker owners, escalation and evidence rather than dashboard-only blocked states.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT transition-scoped idempotency and explicit owner/action into a Blocker object supporting accountable human and Agent assignees, SLA/escalation, durable outbox and resolution evidence.
units.responsibilityConflict: Only an Agent owner is modeled, with no accountable human or escalation. Free-text action and delivery do not prove authority, acknowledgement or blocker resolution.
evidence: 148a5b11 Route blocked transitions to explicit unblock owners (#10112)

units.function: HTTP middleware tests allowing loopback/configured Host headers and rejecting unknown private-deployment hostnames with CLI remediation.
units.dependencyDirection: Request Host/path/Accept and deployment bind/allowlist settings enter middleware before API or page routes; output is pass-through or JSON/plain-text 403.
units.keyDataModels: Enabled flag, bindHost, allowed hostname, Host header and remediation response.
units.lifecycle: Disabled guard allows all; enabled guard permits localhost and allowlisted names, while unknown API/page hosts are blocked and told how to add the hostname.
units.testAssessment: Basic modes, API and page responses are covered. Missing are case/trailing-dot/IDNA/IPv6 normalization, malformed/multiple Host, ports, proxy Forwarded headers, wildcard/subdomain policy, DNS rebinding, CSRF/origin and authorization/audit of allowlist changes.
units.designRationale: Reduce Host-header/DNS-rebinding exposure when a local/private server binds beyond loopback while keeping setup repairable.
units.companyOsProblem: Self-hosted Company OS needs explicit trusted origins/hosts and safe enterprise ingress configuration.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT as a deployment adapter guard with canonical host/origin parsing, trusted-proxy policy, CSRF checks and audited administrator-managed allowlists; never let request headers redefine public links or tenant identity.
units.responsibilityConflict: The error suggests an allowlist mutation but the test does not prove who may perform it or record the resulting security-boundary change.
evidence: 73eb2373 docs: use structured agent mentions in paperclip skill (#4103)

units.function: Security tests for canonical Tool arguments, invocation/tool-bound signatures, dedicated signing-key configuration, sensitive-value summaries and prompt-injection rejection on Tool results.
units.dependencyDirection: Tool name/invocation/arguments and a dedicated environment secret feed signing/verification; untrusted arguments/results enter content validation before summary or return to an Agent.
units.keyDataModels: Canonical arguments, signedArguments, invocationId, toolName, signing secret, content direction, redacted summary/findings and validation errors.
units.lifecycle: Arguments are canonicalized and signed for one invocation/tool, tampering fails and verified bytes parse back. Auth/JWT secrets cannot substitute for the dedicated key. Sensitive fields are redacted from summaries and a recognized prompt-injection result is blocked.
units.testAssessment: Strong focused tests establish domain-separated integrity and early content controls. Missing are canonicalization edge cases, signature algorithm/version/key rotation, constant-time verification, expiry/nonce/replay, Work/approval/data binding, multi-node key custody, schema validation, nested/encoded secrets, prompt-injection false positives/bypasses, quarantine/review and signed result/evidence.
units.designRationale: Prevent a Tool action from changing after inspection and keep malicious/sensitive Tool content from silently flowing into Agent context.
units.companyOsProblem: High-risk actions must bind human approval to exact executable bytes and enforce data/tool firewall policy in the Connector runtime.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT as the leading ActionEnvelope reference: sign canonical action digest with Work/contract/Agent/Connector, human approval, permissions/data scope, policy version, nonce/expiry and expected evidence/result; verify in the execution node, sign outcome, and route suspicious content to quarantine/human review rather than rely only on heuristics.
units.responsibilityConflict: The signature binds invocation/tool/arguments but not who proposed or approved them, the responsible human, Work contract, data authorization or expiry. A shared service secret attests only Paperclip possession and does not prevent authorized replay.
evidence: cfa5e070 feat(mcp) [split 3/8]: add tool access policy core (#9558)

units.function: HTTP regression for returning a clear 400 when an Issue-list URL omits the Company ID segment.
units.dependencyDirection: An Agent-authenticated malformed path reaches Company routes and is rejected before mocked services.
units.keyDataModels: Agent actor, malformed /api/companies/issues path, 400 and corrected path template.
units.lifecycle: The ambiguous route shape is recognized and returns actionable client guidance rather than treating issues as a Company ID.
units.testAssessment: One regression path is covered. Missing are other reserved subpaths, encoded/case variants, service non-invocation assertions, stable error code and OpenAPI/client generation prevention.
units.designRationale: Make a common client routing mistake diagnosable instead of producing misleading downstream behavior.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS APIs need unambiguous organization scoping and structured errors.
units.companyOsFit: REFERENCE the fail-early UX; prefer generated clients, typed route schemas and stable error codes so malformed tenant paths cannot enter domain services.
units.responsibilityConflict: None directly, though tenant IDs must always be verified against authenticated principal authority after parsing.

units.function: Unit tests deriving managed-cloud status and normalized stack metadata from Paperclip-specific environment signals.
units.dependencyDirection: Ambient process environment flows into cloud composition helpers; product features consume a boolean managed floor and optional provisioner metadata.
units.keyDataModels: Tenant server token, managed-config presence, stack ID/slug/account group, primary host/cloud origin and nullable CloudStackContext.
units.lifecycle: A nonblank tenant token or mere presence of managed config marks cloud managed; stray stack metadata outside that state is ignored; managed metadata is trimmed and absent fields remain null.
units.testAssessment: Signal union, blank token and normalization are covered. Missing are malformed origins/hosts/IDs, secret redaction, conflicting sources, explicit deployment profile schema, immutable startup validation, runtime env mutation and feature-level tests proving restrictive behavior cannot weaken.
units.designRationale: Unify two legacy cloud signals without lowering either existing security/restriction floor and expose optional provisioner context.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS must support managed-cloud and self-hosted from one codebase without cloud assumptions entering core or ambiguous ambient configuration changing responsibility semantics.
units.companyOsFit: REFERENCE the restrictive migration rule only. Use an explicit validated DeploymentProfile at the composition root, adapter-specific stack metadata and immutable startup configuration; core/application see capabilities, not Paperclip environment variables.
units.responsibilityConflict: Presence of an empty environment value can switch the product into managed semantics without an accountable deployment decision or signed configuration. Ambient mode inference is insufficient for identity/data-lifecycle responsibility.
